config.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled

intro.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with two input fields to explore controlled and uncontrolled components in React. You'll learn how controlled components manage form data through React state, while uncontrolled components rely on the DOM directly. The core programming concepts include using React state with the useState hook, handling events like onChange, and accessing DOM elements via refs. By the end, you'll understand when to use each approach and implement both in a functional React component.
intro.usecase: Controlled vs uncontrolled components is a fundamental React pattern that appears in nearly every interactive UI. In real software products, controlled components are essential for forms where you need instant validation and feedback—like login screens that show password requirements as you type. Uncontrolled components work well for simple inputs where you only need the final value, such as search filters that submit on enter or file upload inputs. Understanding when to use each approach helps developers build more efficient dashboards, settings panels, and data entry interfaces with appropriate state management.

objectives: Implement a controlled input component by binding its value to React state
Construct an uncontrolled input component using the useRef hook
Manipulate form data by updating state in response to input changes
Initialize form values by setting default state for controlled inputs
Integrate form submission logic that accesses both controlled and uncontrolled values
Render a form that demonstrates the behavioral differences between controlled and uncontrolled inputs
Configure a form with mixed controlled and uncontrolled input strategies

steps.title: Initialize state for controlled input
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'controlledValue' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState('') and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your App component will have a state variable called 'controlledValue' initialized to an empty string, ready to control an input field.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the state variable is named 'controlledValue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with an empty string and naming the variable 'controlledValue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the App component, use useState('') to create a state variable named 'controlledValue'.

steps.title: Create a change handler for controlled input
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named 'handleControlledChange' that takes an event parameter and updates the 'controlledValue' state with event.target.value.
steps.hint: Define a function that receives an event and calls setControlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleControlledChange is defined inside the App component that updates the controlledValue state when called with an event.
successCriteria: The handleControlledChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setControlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named exactly 'handleControlledChange', takes an event parameter, and calls setControlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The change handler function isn't quite right. Remember to create a function named 'handleControlledChange' that updates the controlledValue state using setControlledValue(event.target.value).

steps.title: Add a controlled input field
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your App component, add an <input> element. Set its value attribute to the controlledValue state variable and its onChange attribute to the handleControlledChange handler function.
steps.hint: The input element should be placed inside the <div> in your return statement. Remember to use curly braces for JavaScript expressions in JSX attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The input field will be controlled by React state, meaning its value is always synchronized with the controlledValue state variable.
successCriteria: An <input> element is added inside the <div> with value={controlledValue} and onChange={handleControlledChange} attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but it might not be fully controlled. Make sure you've set both the value and onChange attributes correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field isn't properly controlled. Check that you've added an <input> element with both value and onChange attributes set to the correct variables.

successCriteria: A paragraph element displays 'Controlled value: ' followed by the controlledValue state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your paragraph includes both the static text 'Controlled value: ' and the dynamic controlledValue state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element isn't displaying the controlled input value correctly. Check that you're using JSX curly braces to embed the state value.

steps.title: Create a ref for uncontrolled input
steps.instruction: Import useRef from 'react' and create a ref named 'uncontrolledInputRef' using useRef() inside your component.
steps.hint: Add the import statement at the top, then declare the ref inside the component before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have both useState and useRef imported, and a ref variable declared inside the component.
successCriteria: useRef is imported from 'react' and a ref named 'uncontrolledInputRef' is created with useRef().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: Use the ref attribute to connect the input to the ref you created earlier. The defaultValue attribute sets the initial value without React controlling it.

steps.hint: Define a function inside your component that calls setControlledValue with an empty string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleResetControlled is defined that resets the controlled input's state.
successCriteria: The function handleResetControlled is defined and calls setControlledValue('')
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named handleResetControlled and calls setControlledValue with an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't defined correctly. Check the name and ensure it resets the state.

steps.title: Add a reset button for controlled input
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Reset Controlled' and set its onClick handler to 'handleResetControlled' inside your component's return statement.
steps.hint: Place the button element in the JSX, similar to how you added the controlled input field earlier. Use the onClick attribute to call your reset handler function.

<button onClick={handleReset}>Reset Value</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Reset Controlled' appears below the controlled input field. When clicked, it clears the controlled input value.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Reset Controlled' and onClick set to 'handleResetControlled' is added to the JSX.
